examples.title: 1. LOAD pair split by an independent instruction
examples.description: Two loads from A+0 and A+8 (same 64-byte region) are separated by an unrelated ADD.
examples.expected: L2 is moved directly after L1; the ADD stays after the pair. +1 consecutive opportunity.
examples.dependencies: ADD reads R3,R4 and writes R2 - it shares no register or memory with L2.
examples.source:
; a[0] and a[1] are loaded, an unrelated add sits in between
L1: LOAD R1, [A+0]
ADD R2, R3, R4
L2: LOAD R5, [A+8]
ADD R6, R1, R5

examples.title: 2. STORE pair split by an independent instruction
examples.description: Stores to B+0 and B+8 are separated by a MUL that touches neither.
examples.expected: S2 is moved directly after S1. +1 consecutive opportunity.
examples.dependencies: MUL writes R6; S2 reads R2 and writes B+8. No conflicts.
examples.source:
S1: STORE [B+0], R1
MUL R6, R7, R8
S2: STORE [B+8], R2

examples.title: 3. Intervening STORE to the same location
examples.description: L2 reads A+8, but the catalyst store S1 writes A+8 first.
examples.expected: Rejected: hoisting L2 above S1 would read the old value (MEM-RAW, MUST_ALIAS).
examples.dependencies: S1 -> L2 memory RAW dependence (identical bytes A+8..A+16).
examples.source:
L1: LOAD R1, [A+0]
S1: STORE [A+8], R2
L2: LOAD R3, [A+8]

examples.title: 4. RAW register dependency (pointer chasing)
examples.description: L1 loads a new pointer into R4; L2's address is computed from that loaded value.
examples.expected: Not a valid pair: the tail's use-def chain contains the head (RAW/ADDRESS L1 -> L2), and the distance between the two addresses cannot be proven.
examples.dependencies: L1 -> L2 ADDRESS (RAW on R4). ADD R6 is independent.
examples.source:
; linked list: R4 = node->next, then read a field of the NEW node
L1: LOAD R4, [R4+0]
ADD R6, R6, 1
L2: LOAD R5, [R4+8]

examples.title: 5. Tail address computed late (use-def chain hoisting)
examples.description: The tail's address register R4 is produced by an ADDR in the catalyst. CAIF must hoist that ADDR above the head together with the tail. Uses target 'Cons' because the two loads use different base registers (R3 vs R4) whose distance is still provable (both point into A).
examples.expected: ADDR R4 and L2 are hoisted; MUL (which depends on the head) stays behind. Switch the target to ConsSBR64 to see it rejected as 'different base register'.
examples.dependencies: ADDR R4 -> L2 (ADDRESS). L1 -> MUL (RAW on R1). L1 and L2 are independent.
examples.source:
ADDR R3, A, 0
L1: LOAD R1, [R3+0]
MUL R2, R1, R1        ; uses the head's result -> must stay after the head
ADDR R4, A, 16        ; address of the tail
L2: LOAD R5, [R4+0]

examples.title: 6. Accesses outside the 64-byte window
examples.description: A+0 and A+128 belong to the same array but are 136 bytes apart in span.
examples.expected: Not compatible: span 136 B > 64 B window. Nothing moves.
examples.source:
L1: LOAD R1, [A+0]
ADD R2, R3, R4
L2: LOAD R5, [A+128]

examples.title: 7. Already consecutive pair
examples.description: The compiler already emitted the two loads back to back.
examples.expected: Recognised as an existing opportunity; no movement. Before = after = 1.
examples.dependencies: ADD R3 depends on both loads (RAW); the STORE depends on ADD.
examples.source:
L1: LOAD R1, [A+0]
L2: LOAD R2, [A+8]
ADD R3, R1, R2
S1: STORE [B+0], R3

examples.title: 8. Unknown (possibly aliasing) pointers
examples.description: L1/L2 share base R10, but the catalyst stores through R11, which may point anywhere. L3/L4 use different unknown pointers R12 and R13.
examples.expected: L1+L2 rejected (S1 MAY_ALIAS with L2). L3+L4 not even compatible (distance unprovable).
examples.dependencies: S1 -> L2 MEMORY (MAY_ALIAS). Conservative analysis must assume overlap.
examples.source:
L1: LOAD R1, [R10+0]
S1: STORE [R11+0], R5     ; R11 is a function argument: may alias R10
L2: LOAD R2, [R10+8]
L3: LOAD R3, [R12+0]
L4: LOAD R4, [R13+8]

examples.title: 9. Multiple candidate pairs (unrolled dot product)
examples.description: A 2x unrolled body of c = a[i]*b[i] + a[i+1]*b[i+1]. Loads from A and B are interleaved, so no two compatible loads are adjacent.
examples.expected: Three new consecutive pairs: (L1,L3) on A, (L2,L4) on B and (S1,S2) on C (the ADD computing S2's value is hoisted with it).
examples.dependencies: MULs depend on their loads; ADD R7 on both MULs; S1 on ADD R7; S2 on ADD R8.
examples.source:
L1: LOAD R1, [A+0]
L2: LOAD R2, [B+0]
MUL R3, R1, R2
L3: LOAD R4, [A+8]
L4: LOAD R5, [B+8]
MUL R6, R4, R5
ADD R7, R3, R6
S1: STORE [C+0], R7
ADD R8, R1, R4
S2: STORE [C+8], R8

examples.title: 10. Multiple dependency constraints (WAR, CALL, success)
examples.description: Three candidate pairs, each facing a different constraint.
examples.expected: (L1,L2) rejected by WAR on R2; (L3,L4) rejected because L4 cannot cross the CALL; (S1,S2) succeeds - MOV R9 is independent.
examples.dependencies: ADD R6 reads R2 before L2 overwrites it (WAR). CALL is a memory barrier.
examples.source:
L1: LOAD R1, [A+0]
ADD R6, R2, 1          ; still needs the OLD value of R2
L2: LOAD R2, [A+8]     ; overwrites R2 -> WAR with the ADD
L3: LOAD R3, [B+0]
CALL helper            ; may read/write any memory
L4: LOAD R4, [B+8]
S1: STORE [D+0], R1
MOV R9, 0
S2: STORE [D+16], R3

examples.title: 11. STORE whose value is computed in the catalyst
examples.description: The tail stores R4 = C[0] + R3. Its use-def chain (LOAD R2 and ADD R4) is hoisted above the head.
examples.expected: Chain {I1 (LOAD R2), I3 (ADD R4)} moves above S1; S2 follows S1; the unrelated MUL stays behind.
examples.dependencies: LOAD R2 -> ADD R4 -> S2 (RAW). The chain load reads C, the head writes B: NO_ALIAS.
examples.source:
S1: STORE [B+0], R1
LOAD R2, [C+0]
MUL R7, R8, R8
ADD R4, R2, R3
S2: STORE [B+8], R4

examples.title: 12. Use-def chain load conflicts with a catalyst store
examples.description: Like Fig. 5 of the paper: the tail's chain contains a load, and a catalyst store through an unknown pointer may alias both that load and the tail.
examples.expected: Rejected: MEM-RAW (store -> chain load) and MEM-WAW (store -> tail) may-alias dependences.
examples.dependencies: S9 -> I1 (MEM-RAW, MAY_ALIAS), S9 -> S2 (MEM-WAW, MAY_ALIAS).
examples.source:
S1: STORE [B+0], R1
S9: STORE [R9+0], R2   ; unknown pointer
LOAD R3, [C+0]          ; value for the tail
S2: STORE [B+8], R3

examples.title: 13. Candidates in different basic blocks
examples.description: A conditional branch separates the loads. CAIF never moves code across block boundaries.
examples.expected: No pair is formed across the branch; nothing moves.
examples.dependencies: CMP -> BEQ (RAW on FLAGS). Loads are in blocks B0, B1 and 'done'.
examples.source:
L1: LOAD R1, [A+0]
CMP R1, 0
BEQ done
L2: LOAD R2, [A+8]
done:
L3: LOAD R3, [A+16]
